definitions.gloss: fallen leaves; shedding of leaves; leaf fall
definitions.explanation: The natural process of leaves falling from trees, or the fallen leaves themselves. A more literary or formal term compared to {落|お}ち{葉|ば}.
Used as a modifier to describe trees or forests that shed their leaves seasonally, as opposed to evergreen trees.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}になると{落葉|らくよう}が{始|はじ}まる。
examples.english: Leaf fall begins when autumn arrives.

examples.japanese: {公園|こうえん}の{地面|じめん}が{落葉|らくよう}で{覆|おお}われている。
examples.english: The ground in the park is covered with fallen leaves.

examples.japanese: {街路|がいろ}を{彩|いろど}っていた{並木|なみき}が{落葉|らくよう}し、{冬|ふゆ}の{訪|おとず}れを{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: The trees lining the street shed their leaves, and I felt the arrival of winter.

examples.japanese: {落葉樹|らくようじゅ}は{冬|ふゆ}に{葉|は}を{落|お}とす。
examples.english: Deciduous trees drop their leaves in winter.

examples.japanese: この{森|もり}は{落葉|らくよう}{広葉樹|こうようじゅ}が{中心|ちゅうしん}だ。
examples.english: This forest consists mainly of deciduous broad-leaved trees.

examples.japanese: {落葉樹|らくようじゅ}と{常緑樹|じょうりょくじゅ}が{混|ま}ざった{林|はやし}は、{季節|きせつ}ごとに{違|ちが}う{表情|ひょうじょう}を{見|み}せてくれる。
examples.english: A forest with a mix of deciduous and evergreen trees shows a different face with each season.

notes:
USAGE:
The same kanji {落葉|おちば} read as おちば is the everyday word for fallen leaves. The reading らくよう is more formal/literary and also serves as a botanical/scientific term (deciduous).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {落葉樹|らくようじゅ} (deciduous tree)
- {落葉|らくよう}{広葉樹|こうようじゅ} (deciduous broad-leaved tree)
- {落葉|らくよう}{樹林|じゅりん} (deciduous forest)

CONTRAST:
- {落葉|らくよう} (らくよう): literary/botanical — formal register, used in science and writing
- {落|お}ち{葉|ば} (おちば): everyday — the word most people use in daily life for fallen leaves
- {常緑|じょうりょく}: evergreen — the opposite of deciduous
